s0401.literal: Wugu presumptively established [his rule] in Long'an year 1 of Emperor An; through Rutan's three generations, altogether nineteen years; [the state] was destroyed in Yixi year 10 of Emperor An.
s0401.idiomatic: Wugu claimed kingship in Long'an 1 of Emperor An; three generations later, under Rutan, the line had lasted nineteen years when it fell in Yixi 10 of Emperor An.

s0403.literal: The historiographer says: The Tufa for generation upon generation were tribal chiefs who dominated the borderlands, strung bows at Jade Pass and vaulted horses at Golden Mountain, waited for the full moon to spy on troops and rode the season of broken bow-glue to loose arrows—court ritual did not reach them, imperial teaching was thereby blocked.
s0403.idiomatic: The historian writes: For generations the Tufa were frontier chiefs who ruled the marches. They strung bows at Jade Pass and rode at Golden Mountain, raided under the full moon and shot when the cold made bow-glue snap—court ritual never touched them, and the throne's teaching never reached them.

s0404.literal: Wugu adopted Fu Hun's plan, trained troops to punish the unsubmissive;
s0404.idiomatic: Wugu took Fu Hun's counsel, drilled his armies, and punished rebels;

s0405.literal: Lilugu followed Shi Gao's words, established schools and extended [instruction] to the royal sons.
s0405.idiomatic: Lilugu heeded Shi Gao, founded schools, and brought up the sons of the nobility.

s0406.literal: Thus they could open territory in the lands west of the river and balance against a strong state.
s0406.idiomatic: So they opened lands west of the Yellow River and stood as equals against great powers.

s0407.literal: The Way is enlarged through men—is this not what is meant!
s0407.idiomatic: The Way advances through men—here was the proof.

s0408.literal: Rutan inherited the edge of repeated victories and borrowed the resources of his two elder brothers, smashed the Lü clan with schemes leaving nothing untried, took Guzang without blood on the blades—martial design and heroic plan, matching the tracks of former exemplars.
s0408.idiomatic: Rutan rode the sharp edge of repeated victories and his brothers' legacy, outschemed the house of Lü, and took Guzang without drawing a blade—his martial vision matched the great kings of old.

s0409.literal: Then he improperly usurped a weighty position; fullness easily meets its term; he exhausted troops to vent his heart and let wickedness invite its own harm—land was taken by Mengxun, momentum was checked by Helian—ruined state and lost life, and even that was fortunate.
s0409.idiomatic: Then he clung to a throne too heavy for him; fullness invites ruin. He spent armies to feed his pride and wickedness to destroy himself—Mengxun seized his lands, Helian broke his power. To lose realm and life was still a mercy.

s0410.literal: In old times Duke Shang of Song loved war and brought disaster upon Hua Du;
s0410.idiomatic: Long ago Duke Shang of Song loved war and brought ruin on Hua Du;

s0411.literal: King Ling of Chu doted on arms and met killing at Ganxi.
s0411.idiomatic: King Ling of Chu doted on arms and died at Ganxi.

s0412.literal: Different ages, same ruin—in Rutan this is seen.
s0412.idiomatic: Different ages, the same end—so it was with Rutan.

s0413.literal: Praise says: Tufa brothers dominated the barbarian hosts.
s0413.idiomatic: The eulogy says: The Tufa brothers ruled the frontier tribes.

s0414.literal: They opened territory beyond the river and cleared the miasma of the western lands.
s0414.idiomatic: They carved a realm beyond the river and cleared the western sky.

s0415.literal: Rutan stood out, vaulting over the heroes of the time.
s0415.idiomatic: Rutan rose above the heroes of his age.

s0416.literal: Exhausting troops and doting on war—ruined state and fallen fame.
s0416.idiomatic: He spent his armies on war—realm lost, name in ruins.
